/itineraryStops/5/whyOnRoute.source_en: The ⟦G0⟧-vs-Jogyesa choice covers the two most natural 'last hour in Seoul' frames: 'shop and eat' vs 'reflect and absorb.' Picked over forcing a single venue because the customizable choice IS the private-tour value proposition — group bus tours can't offer this binary in-the-moment decision. For cruise guests, the ⟦G0⟧-Jogyesa choice is the day's most flexible private-charter advantage — your driver-guide reads the group's energy level and interest at ~16:00 and routes to whichever venue fits (⟦G0⟧'s bustle for shoppers/foodies; Jogyesa's calm for cultural depth). The choice is impossible on bus tours where the route is fixed before departure.

/itineraryStops/5/description.source_en:
The day's final substantive stop is YOUR CHOICE between two distinct Seoul finales: **OPTION A — ⟦G1⟧**: Seoul's #1 shopping and K-beauty district in Jung-gu. Pedestrian-friendly zone with restricted vehicle access. Major Korean cosmetics flagships (Innisfree, Etude House, Laneige, Olive Young, Missha) with generous free samples. 

⟦G1⟧ Cathedral (built 1898 — Korea's first brick Gothic Catholic church, played significant role in democratization movement). Lotte Department Store flagship (1970s, multi-floor luxury including Avenuel designer wing). Street food: tornado potato skewers, hotteok pancakes, egg bread, cheesy corn dogs, tanghulu sugar-glazed fruit skewers. 

CASH-ONLY at most street stalls (bring 20,000 KRW). Open daily; shops 10:30-22:00, street food 12:00-22:00 (later on weekends). **OPTION B — ⟦G0⟧**: Head temple of the Jogye Order — Korea's largest Buddhist Order. Origins back to 1395 (Gakhwangsa); modern temple founded 1910; renamed Jogyesa in 1954 after the Buddhist Purification Movement. 

Daeungjeon (Main Dharma Hall) is the largest temple building in Seoul. Natural Monument No. 9: 500-year-old Baeksong (Lacebark/White Pine, 14 m tall, 1.85 m trunk). 450-year-old Chinese Scholar Tree. 

Ten-story stone pagoda housing 10 Buddha sari gifted by Thai royal court. FREE admission. Annual Lotus Lantern Festival around Buddha's Birthday (May) is UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage — temple courtyard fills with thousands of paper lanterns. 

The only major traditional temple in Seoul's city center (most Korean temples are in mountains). 5-min walk to ⟦G2⟧. Your driver-guide takes you to whichever option fits your group's interests — ⟦G1⟧ for shoppers/foodies; Jogyesa for cultural/spiritual depth.

/itineraryStops/5/visitBasics/hours.source_en: ⟦G0⟧: shops 10:30-22:00, street food 12:00-22:00. Jogyesa: grounds 24/7, main halls 06:00-18:00

/itineraryStops/5/visitBasics/admission.source_en: Both FREE (⟦G0⟧ purchases pay-as-you-go; Jogyesa fee-free)
